# Measured COMSOL 6.2 / MPh API rules (106 rules, 106 distinct names)

Every rule below was measured on the rig (round cited inline). A rule with no citation is a defect.

## 2. Rules (each measured; the measurement is cited)

- **R-RC — never trust `comsolbatch`'s exit code.** It is 0 on a thrown exception (`j0`). Read
  `<input>.class.status` line 2 (`Done`/`Error`) and the batch log's `/*****Error********/` block.
  `batch_verdict.py` is the only accepted reader. (Carrier J only; M raises Python exceptions.)
- **R-FS — batch runs the class inside COMSOL's methods security manager.** Every file write
  (`table.save`, `export().run`, `model.save(path)`, `java.io.FileWriter`) throws
  `AccessControlException`. Run `comsolbatch … -prefsdir <per-run dir>` whose `comsol.prefs`
  is the user's copy plus `security.external.filepermission=full`. Never edit
  `~/.comsol/v62/comsol.prefs`. Rejected values: `all`, `off`, `limited`. Fallback (whole
  restriction set off): `security.external.enable=off`. (j1b × prefs.)
- **R-EXPORT — `Plot` export is banned.** A 1D `LineGraph` plot export reports success and writes
  nothing under both carriers (m4 A/B/C). Use `Data` export (`set("data",dset); set("expr",[...]);
  set("filename",…)`) or `numerical(...).setResult()` → `table(...).save(path)`. Refined by R-EXPORT-PLOT-TEXT (round 21):
  on solved seeds `Global` and `LineGraph` plot exports DO write — the m4 case is the unexplained one; and figures
  themselves are reachable through an `Image` export node (R-IMAGE-EXPORT).
- **R-THROWS — `.java` entry points declare `throws Exception`** (`run()` and `main()`), or
  `comsolcompile` fails on the checked `IOException` of `model.save` / `table.save`.
- **R-CTRL — every study script carries its own positive and negative control** and prints both
  values; a script that can only pass is not evidence (brief A catalog rule, unchanged).
- **R-READ — export parsing is not rewritten.** The source's `sci-analysis-pipeline` project (a private tree on a non-system drive) — `sap.ingest.read_comsol`
  reads both table and grid shapes (verified on m2, j1b W1, j1b W4).
- **R-TAG — inputs carry their provenance tag; outputs carry a label.** Untagged number = defect;
  unlabeled result = not reportable (brief A README, unchanged).
- **R-JPYPE — integer property values go through `jpype.JInt(n)`.** A bare Python `int` in
  `node.set("prop", 2)` raises `Ambiguous overloads (int/double/boolean)`; strings and lists are fine.
  (S2 build, `HeteroModelSelection`, `elemcount`.)
- **R-DEFAULT-TAGS — physics interfaces ship default features whose tags are taken.** `semi` already owns
  `cont1` (Continuity) and `smm1`; creating a feature with a default tag throws "already exists". Use
  study-specific tags (`hj1`, `adm7`, …), never `cont1`/`smm1`/`init1`. (S2 build.)
- **R-FIELD — read the electric field as `semi.normE`, never `-d(V,x)`.** On the solved semi dataset
  `-d(V,x)` evaluated to exactly 0 for every node and every Va while `semi.normE` gave 0–188 kV/cm;
  `semi.Ex` does not exist in 1D. A zero field is an instrument fault (S2 gate I1 caught it), not a result.
- **R-EXPORT-SIZE — a `Data` export over a parameter sweep writes every solution as extra columns**
  (S2: 51 Va × 5 expressions × 5253 nodes = 33 MB per variant). Restrict with the export node's
  solution selection, or export only the expressions the gate reads.
- **R-1D-SEL — in 1D, entity numbers are ordinal in coordinate order** (`Interval` with n+1 coords →
  domains 1..n, boundaries 1..n+1) and the script asserts the counts. Measured on S2. 2D/3D still OPEN below.
- **R-SEL — 2D/3D selections are coordinate boxes in the geometry sequence, never entity numbers.**
  MEASURED on S1 (2D periodic cell, 12 stacked rectangles, 37 boundaries, `08_S1_absorption-vs-SiN/probe3.log`):
  `geom.create(tag,"BoxSelection")` with `entitydim` (`jpype.JInt`), `xmin/xmax/ymin/ymax` as
  parameter expressions (`"0+t_sub+t_p_contact-1"`), `condition="inside"`; `UnionSelection` with
  `input=[tags]` merges boxes. Physics, material and coupling nodes reference them as
  `selection().named("geom1_<tag>")` — **no `_dom`/`_bnd` suffix** (the suffixed names were empty or
  raised). Each reference prints `selection().entities()` and the script asserts the expected count
  (materials `[1,8,9,10]`, port `[2]`, 24 side boundaries, top `[25]`). Because bounds are expressions,
  a swept thickness (`t_SiN` 10→600 nm) never touches the selections. `model.component().selection()`
  ("Box" outside the geometry) was not needed and stays unmeasured.
- **R-FEATURE-NAMES — feature type ids differ from GUI names.** `Scattering` (not
  `ScatteringBoundaryCondition`), `Port`, `PeriodicCondition`, `EvalGlobal`; the ewfd wave equation
  is `wee1` with `DisplacementFieldModel=RefractiveIndex`. When unsure, save the nearest seed as
  `.java` (stage S1) and copy the id. An unknown id raises `Unknown feature ID` immediately (cheap).
- **R-LIST-ACCESS — feature lists are indexed through the PARENT accessor, never through the list object.**
  `m.result().numerical("tag")`, `m.component("comp1").material("tag")`, `m.component("comp1").physics("tag")`;
  the list returned by `material()` is neither callable nor has `.feature()` (`…ListClient object is not callable`,
  `…has no attribute 'feature'`). Only nodes (a physics interface, a geometry, a mesh) expose `.feature("tag")`.
- **R-RESERVED-NAMES — parameter names must not shadow COMSOL variables.** `h` (mesh size) raised
  "Duplicate parameter/variable name" at compile; also avoid `x y z t r`, `pi`, `*_const`. Prefix every
  parameter (`t_core`, `w_core`, `n_clad`). (U1.)
- **R-EVALGLOBAL-SHAPE — `EvalGlobal.getReal()` is [expression][solution].** One expression → `ravel()` is safe;
  several → `reshape(n_expr, -1)` and pick the column of the wanted eigen/parameter solution. (U1 Si strip.)
- **R-SAVE-JAVA — seed → text needs the two-argument form `model.java.save(path, "java")`.** The one-argument
  `save("x.java")` writes `.mph` content under a `.java` name (grep reports "binary file"). (U1 seed conversion.)
- **R-MODES — mode analysis returns box/cladding modes and polarization pairs.** Count guided modes as distinct
  `real(ewfd.neff)` (tolerance 1e-5) that exceed the cladding index by more than 1e-4; degenerate pairs count once.
  Study: `ModeAnalysis` with `modeFreq`, `neigsactive/neigs` (`jpype.JInt`), `shiftactive/shift = n_core`.
  Field read-out: `Interp` numerical node, `setInterpolationCoordinates(JArray(JDouble,2)([xs, ys]))`, `set("solnum", k)`.
  MFD gate uses Marcuse's definition (overlap-maximising Gaussian), not a least-squares fit. (U1.)

- **R-ISOLATE — a FAIL that may come from an `[X?]` input is isolated before it is reported.** S1: period and
  amplitudes matched the paper, the extremum sat 90 nm off. Before declaring, the script `s1b_phase_isolation.py`
  wrote its hypothesis down (which input moves the position, which observable must NOT move), swept only that
  input, and reported both controls: amplitude control PASS (spread 0.005), analytic slope control FAIL
  (−1.94 vs −1.58 estimate). The verdict stays FAIL; the README says what the FAIL is made of. Widening the
  tolerance until it passes is the named anti-pattern.
- **R-GLOBAL-READ — global scalars come from `result().numerical().create(tag,"EvalGlobal")` + `getReal()`**,
  read through `numerical(tag)`; `MPh.evaluate` is used for spatial fields only (S2) — one mechanism per shape.

- **R-CORES — start the Comsol session with `mph.start(cores=8)` on this machine; never the logical count.**
  Measured (`01_environment/bench_cores.jsonl`, Ryzen 9 8940HX 16C/32T laptop, 2026-09-13): 1D semi sweep
  15.7 / 9.0 / 9.0 / 13.5 / 30.8 s at 1 / 4 / 8 / 16 / 32 cores; 2D ewfd 162 k elements 12.7 / 11.1 / 11.3 / 13.0 s
  at 1 / 4 / 8 / 16. `-blas aocl` and `-mpmode throughput` gave no gain (±1 s). Hyperthreads (32) double the time.
  `cores=1` (used by S2/S1 runs) costs ~1.7× on the semi model. Re-measure with `bench_cores.py --cores N` when a
  model is 3D or > 1 M DOF — the optimum may move up. **No GPU path exists in 6.2** (GPU solvers arrived in
  6.3 acoustics / 6.4 cuDSS; no CUDA library in the install), so the RTX 5070 is irrelevant to this pipeline.

- **R-SEMI-2D — a 2D `semi` study starts with a `SemiconductorEquilibrium` step, then `Stationary` with the
  voltage sweep.** Without it Newton fails at the initial parameter ("Failed to find a solution for the initial
  parameter", U3 run4) although the same stack solves in 1D. SRH lifetimes: `TrapAssistedRecombination` feature with
  `taun_mat="userdef"` + `taun` (the material-group route needs the `SRH` property group, not `SemicondMaterial`;
  `smm1` has no `taun`). Gate oxide: `GateContact` boundary with `V0`, `epsilon_ins`, `d_ins`. Doping:
  `AnalyticDopingModel` with `impurityType` and `NDc`/`NAc`. Field maximum + location: `Maximum` coupling,
  `maxop(semi.normE)` and `maxop(semi.normE, x)`. (U3.)
- **R-INTERP-SWEEP — `Interp` over a parametric sweep: `solnum` takes an integer (`jpype.JInt(k)`), never `"all"`**
  ("This property only supports constant expressions", U3 run5); walk the sweep index explicitly. (U3.)
- **R-SOLVER-SEQ — solver settings copied from a seed (damped Newton, tolerances) go on the auto sequence, which
  must exist first.** `study.createAutoSequences("all")`, then walk `sol(tag).feature(*)` of type `Stationary` and
  its `FullyCoupled` children: `initstep 0.1`, `minstep 1e-4`, `maxiter 50`, `rstep 10`, `dtech "auto"` (the
  `mosfet_breakdown` seed's values). Mesh grading from the seeds too: `hgrad 1.05–1.25`, contact edges 30 nm; a
  5 nm edge size against a 150 nm domain size with `hgrad 1.3` made Newton fail at the first step for every small
  corner radius (U3 run7), and one radius (200 nm) still failed under the seed settings (run8) — convergence of a
  2D `semi` model is mesh-recipe dependent, so a skipped radius is counted, never hidden. (U3 run8.)
- **R-MAXOP-BOUNDARY — a `maxop` maximum that sits on a boundary junction is a mesh quantity.** U3 runs 6–8: the
  global maximum stayed at the symmetry-axis/trench-bottom junction and moved 4415 → 1630 → 2032 → 3064 kV/cm with
  the edge mesh, while a sampling line 10 nm inside the semiconductor changed 3.6 % under the same refinement.
  Report `maxop` but gate on `Interp` samples at a fixed offset from the boundary; the crowding maximum on a rounded
  corner sits ~30–40° from the flat bottom, not at the 45° midpoint. (U3.)
- **R-PLANAR-REF — a "far-field / planar" reference point must be farther from the structure than the depletion
  width.** U3 run6: x = 1.9 µm from a trench with a 3.3 µm depletion width read 528 vs 627 kV/cm analytic (−16 %);
  widening the half cell to 6 µm gave 595.5 (−5 %) and closed G1 and U18. (U3.)
- **R-PERTURB-READ — a `Frequencylinearized` (small-signal) solution evaluates the LINEARIZATION POINT by default.**
  `EvalGlobal` on the MOSCAP seed returned the DC gate charge (−2.1 µC-scale "capacitance", U6 run1). The harmonic
  part is selected with the seed plot's own property `numerical.set("differential", True)`; with it on, parameters
  (`freq`, `V0`) evaluate to 0 (their perturbation is zero), so read the sweep coordinates in a second call with
  `differential=False` and pair the columns (U6 run2 → run3 PASS). Seed read-out forms `semi.Q0_2/1[mV]` and
  `-semi.I0_1/semi.iomega/1[mV]` agree to 0.00 %.
- **R-BATCH-SOLS — a batch/"Parametric Sweep" study stores ONE solution object per parameter value.** The seed's
  `optical_ring_resonator` sweep leaves `sol5, sol6, …` (one per `lda0`); the accumulated psol dataset returns only
  the first value, and `EvalGlobal`'s `outersolnum` is an int property that does not iterate (`"all"` → "constant
  expressions only"). Read-out: create a `Solution` dataset per swept `sol` tag, evaluate each, sort by the parameter;
  remove the swept `sol`/dataset tags before the next sweep or stale values leak in (U22 probes 3–6).
- **R-LIB-PREVIEW — not every Application Library `.mph` on disk is a model.** ~30 kB files (`cpw_numeric_tem_port`,
  `gcpw_numeric_tem_port`, `microstrip_line_tem_differential`, …) are download stubs; `client.load` raises "This is
  a COMSOL Application Libraries preview file". Check the file size (real seeds are ≥ 200 kB) before planning a round
  on a seed. (U5.)
- **R-SEL-HOLE / R-SEL-DIFF — two selection forms measured NOT to work.** (1) A strip subtracted from a domain as a
  hole leaves its bottom edge on the substrate top unselectable by any coordinate box (`inside`, `allvertices`,
  `somevertex` all empty; `intersects` returns every y = 0 segment) — keep thin metals as DOMAINS excluded from the
  physics and take their edges with `AdjacentSelection` (input = the domain box; measured OK). (2) `DifferenceSelection`
  with `add`/`subtract` returned the `add` set unchanged; use an `intersects` box that only the wanted domain's
  bounding box meets, or `UnionSelection` of side boxes. (U5 runs 1–2.) Follow-up (runs 3–4): an `intersects` box
  returned every domain too, so domain lists that need a set difference are computed in Python from `inside`-box
  entity numbers read at build time and written back with `selection().set(JArray(JInt)(...))`.
- **R-RESERVED-NAMES-2 (extends R-RESERVED-NAMES) — `s` (boundary arc length), `w`, `t` join `h`.** "Duplicate parameter/variable
  name: s — Boundaries" (U5 run7). Use two-letter parameter names (`wc`, `sg`, `tm`, `h_sub`).
- **R-MODES-RF — 2D `emw` Mode Analysis of a metal cross-section identifies the quasi-TEM mode reliably only with
  metal thick enough for the mesh.** 1 µm strips: n_eff 2.6029 (ε 6.775, +0.11 % vs `es` at the same geometry);
  0.1 µm strips: 2.82 with the default PEC exterior, 2.70 plus a non-physical 3.75 with a PMC exterior. Compare the
  mode route with the electrostatic route at the SAME geometry, and check the gate against the closed form with
  the electrostatic route (thin metal, R-thickness: 1 µm metal lowered ε_eff by −2.3 %, Gupta predicts −2.6 %). (U5.)
- **R-INTERP-UNIT — `Interp` (point evaluation) coordinates are in the GEOMETRY length unit, not SI.** The
  `mesfet` seed declares `geom1.lengthUnit("µm")`; coordinates passed in metres (2e-9 … 5e-7) all collapsed onto
  (0, ~0) and returned one bulk value for every point (V identical to 4 decimals, n = Nd everywhere; U19 run4,
  probe 3). Read `geom.lengthUnit()` first, or write geometry in µm and pass µm. Same applies to `setInterpolationCoordinates` in U3 (there the geometry was already in µm).
- **R-SWEEP-START — a semiconductor parametric sweep must start at a point the seed's initial values can reach.**
  A (Vg, Vd) sweep whose first point was Vd = 0.05 V failed Newton at Nd = 2e16 ("Failed to find a solution for the
  initial parameter"); the same sweep prefixed with Vd = 0 converged in 2 s (U19 probe 2). Deep-pinch-off points
  (past V_T with drain bias applied) also lose convergence — stop a transfer sweep ~0.2 V short of V_T when the
  gate does not need them (U19 run2). Field-variable names differ from the GUI labels: temperature is `semi.T0`,
  `semi.Nc`/`semi.Nv`/`semi.ni` exist, `semi.T`, `semi.n`, `semi.Ne` do not; the electron concentration is `semi.N`.
- **R-STUDY-CHAIN — library seeds chain their studies (`useinitsol`/`initstudy`): run the initialiser first, and map
  datasets to studies instead of assuming `dset<n>` ↔ `std<n>`.** `bipolar_transistor` std2 (Gummel) starts from
  std1's last solution; the mapping that worked: `dataset(tag).getString("solution")` → `sol(tag).feature("st1").getString("study")`.
  A study that swaps a voltage terminal for a current terminal does it with `disabledphysics` on the study step, not
  by editing the physics (U20). Terminal currents keep the seed's sign convention — check the sign before fitting logs.
- **R-GATE-REGIME — a mesh/consistency gate is evaluated in the bias regime the physics gate lives in, never at the
  numerically most sensitive extreme.** U20 run1: β_peak sat at V_BE 0.425 V (I_B ≈ 1e-13 A, SRH-dominated) and moved
  −3.5 % on refinement while β at 0.6 V moved −1.0 % and I_C −1.9 %; the gate window (0.45–0.65 V) is where the ruler
  applies, so the mesh metric is taken there and the peak reported. Same lesson as R-MAXOP-BOUNDARY, other axis.
- **R-INTERP-SHAPE — `Interp.getReal()` is (points × expressions); `EvalGlobal.getReal()` is (expressions × solutions).**
  Reshaping an Interp result the EvalGlobal way interleaves the columns: U7 run4 mixed a constant `nloc` column into
  |E| and every beam width came out as the uniform-field value (103 µm) while the point-by-point profile was a correct
  Gaussian (probe 2). Use `reshape(len(points), len(exprs)).T`; with one expression both forms coincide, which is why
  U3/U19 never saw it.
- **R-EWBE-2D-AMPLITUDE — a 2D out-of-plane Beam Envelopes Gaussian launch takes the 3-vector `Eg0`
  (`["0","0","1[V/m]"]`), not the 3D seed's `Eg0NN`.** Setting only `Eg0NN` launched an identically-zero field with no
  error (U7 run2, probe 1); a scalar `Eg0` is refused ("A vector of length 3 expected", run3). The ewbe default wave
  equation feature is `webe1` (not `wee1`), `IncidentField = "GaussianBeam"`, `w0`, `p0` (focal-plane distance, 0 = waist
  at the boundary), `inputQuantity` defaults to `ElectricFieldAmplitude`. Per-domain wave vector: `k1 = ["k0*nloc","0","0"]`
  with `nloc` a component variable node per domain selection (the `focusing_lens` seed's pattern).
- **R-OPT-SCOPE — an Optimization study step evaluates its objective in GLOBAL scope: a component variable must be
  written `comp1.wq`, bare `wq` is "Undefined variable" (U14 probe 2).** Setup that works: `st.create("opt","Optimization")`,
  `set("optsolver","bobyqa")`, `set("opttol","1e-3")`, `setIndex("optobj", expr, 0)`, `setIndex("pname"/"initval"/"scale"/
  "lbound"/"ubound", value, 0)` (values with units), then `study.run()`. The global parameter is NOT updated afterwards; the
  optimum and every evaluation are in a result table whose header contains `Objective` (`m.result().table(tag)
  .getColumnHeaders()` / `.getReal()`). Measured: 11 evaluations, 62 s for a 6-s model; the bound is returned (not an error)
  when the target is unreachable.
- **R-UQ-KEYVALUE — an UncertaintyQuantification study step's per-input columns are "arrays of alternating keys and
  values": only the full-matrix form `q.set(prop, [["col1", value]])` is accepted; every `setIndex` form is refused and
  the run then fails with empty bounds (U13 run2 / probe 4).** Properties: `distributionselection` (`normal`), `s1selection`
  (mean) and `s2selection` (std), `lboundselection`/`uboundselection`, `punitselection` (`m`) — values in SI WITHOUT unit
  brackets (`"5e-6"`, `"1e-7"`). `setIndex("pname","w0",0)` and `setIndex("qoiexpression","comp1.wq",0)` (component scope,
  as R-OPT-SCOPE) do work. `uqtype` ∈ `uncertaintypropagation` | `screening`; `uqmethod` accepts only `sbmontecarlo`
  (surrogate-based; `montecarlo`/`lhs`/`mc` refused); `surrogatemodel` ∈ `aspce`/`spce`/`agp`/`gp` (default `agp`, `none`
  refused); `nsolve` = number of design points. Output: a design-point table `[pname, qoi]`, a statistics table
  `[Mean, STD, Minimum, Maximum, Lower/Upper 90/95/99 %]` (SI), adaptive-iteration and surrogate-error tables, a
  verification-point table, dataset `kde1`. Measured: 113 s for nsolve 12 (+ adaptive refinement) on a 6-s model. Table
  NUMBERS move with the adaptive iteration count (probe 4: tbl1 = 12 design points; run3: tbl1 = 10 000 surrogate MC
  samples, tbl9 = 20 solved points) — identify tables by their column headers, never by tag.
- **R-3D-PORTS — 3D ewfd/ewbe numeric ports from text (U15 probe 1 + run1):** `create("port1","Port",2)` on a boundary box
  selection, `set("PortType","Numeric")`, `set("PortExcitation","on"/"off")`; the study needs one `BoundaryModeAnalysis`
  step per port (`set("PortName","1")`, `set("modeFreq","f0")`, `set("shiftactive",True)`, `set("shift","n_Si")` → the
  highest-n_eff mode) BEFORE the `Frequency` step, and `study.run()` builds the chained eigen/stationary sequence itself.
  Read-back on `dset1`: `ewfd.beta_1/k0` (port n_eff), `abs(ewfd.S21)^2` = `ewfd.Tport_2`, `abs(ewfd.S11)^2` =
  `ewfd.Rport_1`, `ewfd.S21dB`. Scattering walls: `create("sctr1","Scattering",2)` on a `UnionSelection` of the four wall
  box selections (`set("input",[tags])`, `entitydim` 2 as `jpype.JInt`). A taper is a `WorkPlane` (`quickplane "zx"`,
  `quicky`) + `Polygon` (`source "table"`, `table [[z,x],…]`) + `Extrude` (`setIndex("distance","h_Si",0)`,
  `selection("input").set("wp1")`).
- **R-SWEEP-MESH — swept prism mesh for propagation problems:** `FreeTri` on the source face (with a `Size` sub-feature
  on the core face selection), then `create("swe1","Sweep")` with `selection().all()`, `selection("sourceface").named(…)`,
  `selection("targetface").named(…)`, `create("dis1","Distribution").set("numelem", jpype.JInt(N))`. DOF then scales
  linearly with length (60 layers of 1130 triangles = 67 800 prisms at L = 6 µm, dz 0.1 µm). Free tetrahedra at the same
  sizes were 187 k tets / 1.22 M DOF / 98 s / 7.2 GB peak.
- **R-DOF-MEM — measuring cost:** DOF = `m.sol("sol1").getSize()[0]` after the run; peak memory = the
  `comsolmphserver.exe` child's `psutil … memory_info().peak_wset` (monotone per server → solve ascending sizes, or one
  server per size); `psutil.virtual_memory().available` before the run is the headroom. The mph server holds its peak
  working set until the client exits, so a 13 GB solve leaves 5 GB for anything started next.
- **R-EWBE-3D-PHASE — 3D Beam Envelopes taper:** the 2D `tapered_waveguide` seed pattern works in 3D — `WaveVector`
  `dirCount "UniDirectionality"`, `PhaseSpec "UserDefined"`, `phase1 "phi"`, with component variables
  `kz = ewbe.beta_1 + (ewbe.beta_2 − ewbe.beta_1)·z/L`, `phi = (kz + ewbe.beta_1)·z/2` (port propagation constants are
  available as variables because the BMA steps run first). On the SAME fine free-tet mesh as ewfd it is NOT cheaper
  (13 min, 13.9 GB vs 98 s, 7.2 GB; T 0.99776 vs 0.99846) — the saving only comes from a coarse swept mesh along z.
  Memory is the wall, not DOF: ewbe 3D at L 20 µm took 0.67 M DOF but +20 GB (≈30 GB per M DOF vs ≈5 for ewfd);
  iterative solvers untested.
- **R-CONTROL-OWNED — a positive control is gated on quantities the MODEL produces, never on a closed-form estimate
  chosen after the fact (U15 runs 1–3 + probe 2):** the abrupt-junction control was gated on a guessed threshold (run1),
  then on the scalar-E overlap × n_eff-Fresnel step formula (run2, run3: +20/+21 %), before probe 2 isolated model vs
  ruler — the model was fine (T(step) 0.930/0.930/0.922 for narrow sections 2/6/10 µm; a port within 2 µm of the
  discontinuity changes T by ≤1.5 %), the ruler was wrong (scalar overlap underestimates a Δn_eff 0.76 butt joint by
  21 %; the H-weighted vector overlap |∫E₁×H₂*|²/(P₁₁P₂₂) × Fresnel gives 0.926 vs FEM 0.930). Gate the control on
  loss ratio and separation from the adiabatic case; put every overlap formula in a REPORT line. Three attempts that each
  changed the reference while the geometry stayed suspect is the anti-pattern R-ISOLATE exists to stop.
- **R-IMAGE-EXPORT — figures ARE reachable headlessly: an `Image` export node writes PNG (round 21, probes p1/p2/p2b/p2d).**
  `result().export().create(tag, "Image")`, `set("plotgroup", pg)`, `set("pngfilename", path)`, `run()` — 800×600 by default.
  Pixel size: `size="manualprint"`, `unit="mm"`, `width`/`height` as strings, `resolution` in dpi (160×100 mm @ 200 dpi →
  1260×787); `size="manualweb"` + `widthpx/heightpx/widthexact` are accepted and IGNORED (still 800×600). Decorations
  (axes, colour legend, title): set `options2d=True` (or `options1d`) FIRST, then `axes2d/legend2d/title2d=True` — set
  `options2d` last and the three are reset (p2 s1 blank vs p2d V1 decorated). Geometry and mesh images: `sourcetype=
  "geometry"|"mesh"` + `sourceobject="geom1"|"mesh1"` (no plot group needed); a `Mesh` plot feature in a 2D plot group
  also works. `unit="cm"` and `background="white"` are rejected (`background` ∈ current/fromtheme/color/transparent).
  Per-solution frames of a parametric/transient plot group: `pg.set("looplevel", [i_level0, i_level1, …])` with ONE
  string index per parameter level (mosfet pg3 on dset2: `["11","3"]` = Vd index 11, Vg index 3; a one-entry array on a
  two-level dataset raises "array of strings that can be integers" — p2c); transient datasets have one level. The
  rendered 2D image carries the plot group's own title/legend (log colour bar, min/max markers) — what the GUI shows.
- **R-EXPORT-PLOT-TEXT (refines R-EXPORT, round 21) — `Plot` TEXT export is not banned, it is dataset-shape-dependent.** m3/m4 measured a
  LineGraph on a from-text 1D model writing nothing; on the solved seeds a `Global` plot export wrote 790 B (mosfet, p1 E)
  and 7 460 B, and a `LineGraph` on a `CutLine2D` wrote 199 689 B (pn_diode_circuit, run2 REPORT). The m3 case is now
  the unexplained one (1D model, no cut line). Keep `Data` export / `numerical → table.save` as the primary route;
  `Plot` export is usable once its file size is checked > 0 in the same run.
- **R-RESULT-ACCESS — node LISTS are not callable (round 21, p1/p2, 2 probes lost).** `m.result()`, `m.result().export()`
  and `m.result().numerical()` return list clients; `m.result()(tag)` / `ex(tag)` raise "object is not callable". Address
  nodes as `m.result(tag)`, `m.result().export(tag)`, `m.result().numerical(tag)`. MPh's own `model.export(name, path)`
  addresses nodes by LABEL, not tag (`Node "exports/imgC" does not exist`) — use the Java node for tagged exports.
- **R-INTERP-SHAPE-MULTI (re-measured R-INTERP-SHAPE, round 21 run2) — a multi-expression `Interp` read reshaped as `(n_expr, -1)` interleaves the
  expressions.** `getReal()` is points × expressions: `reshape(-1, n_expr).T`. Symptom: a moiré field map and a
  potential colour bar reading 1e25 V; single-expression reads (gates) were unaffected, so the figure route caught what
  the gates could not — a figure gate needs a model read of the raster, not just "PNG exists".
- **R-NEWTON-MAXITER — the shipped `pn_diode_circuit` transient does not converge headlessly as shipped (round 21, p3/p3b).**
  Manual BDF step tmax/100 with `fc1 maxiter 4` fails "Nonlinear solver did not converge" at t = 17 µs under both
  `study.run()` and `sol("sol1").runAll()`; `fc1.set("maxiter", jpype.JInt(25))` alone converges (173–204 s, 41 347 DOF).
  The tutorial's own stationary-initial-step remedy (pdf p.4) was not needed. A bare int here raises R-JPYPE's
  "Ambiguous overloads (boolean/int/double)" — p3 B/C were lost to it.
- **R-T0-ARTEFACT — a transient seed that starts from a zero initial guess carries an unphysical t = 0 sample (round 21).**
  pn_diode_circuit: V_load(0) −0.544 V, V_diode(0) +0.544 V with a 0 V source; from the first step on the negative half
  is |V_load| < 1.3e-5 V. Gate transient quantities on t > 0 and REPORT the t = 0 sample; the tutorial documents the
  cause (no stationary initial step) — a stationary step before the transient is the untested cure.
- **R-CONTACT-POTENTIAL — `V` at a Metal Contact is not the terminal voltage (round 21 run2 F4).** The electric potential
  difference anode−cathode at the forward peak read −0.013 V while the circuit saw +0.866 V: `V` carries each contact's
  equilibrium offset, so contact-to-contact `V` includes the built-in potential (≈0.88 V here). Compare CHANGES relative
  to a zero-bias solution, or read the terminal variables (`semi.V0_1`, `cir.*_v`).
- **R-NNETDOP-SIGN — `semi.Nnetdop` reads as a magnitude in these seeds (round 21 run2).** Over the p-substrate of the
  MOSFET and the p-region of the diode it returned +1e17 (the seeds' own net-doping plot groups split the sign with
  `semi.Na-semi.Nd > 1` filters). For a signed map read `semi.Nd-semi.Na` explicitly.

- **R-IMAGE-EXPORT-3D — 3D plot groups export like 2D ones, but the decoration keys differ (round 22, probes p1/p2).**
  `axes3d`, `axisorientation3d` and `grid3d` do NOT exist on an `Image` export node ("Unknown property"); `options3d`,
  `legend3d`, `title3d`, `logo3d` do. The 3D PNG carries the plot group's view (camera, axes, grid, colour bar) as
  the GUI would draw it; 160×120 mm @ 200 dpi → 1260×866 (plot group) or 1102×945 (geometry/mesh via `sourcetype`).
  A plot group that reads a study the round did not run exports an EMPTY frame (axes only) that still passes a
  pixel-std blank check (bjt pg4/pg5, run1) — the figure self-read catches it, the checker does not.
- **R-CPL-CREATE-GEOM — `m.cpl().create(tag, "Integration")` raises "Undefined create method"; the geometry argument is
  required: `m.cpl().create(tag, "Integration", "geom1")` (round 22, p2/run1).** Then `.selection().geom("geom1",
  jpype.JInt(2))` + `.selection().named("geom1_<sel>")`, `.set("opname", …)`. Geometry selections also need
  `jpype.JInt` for `entitydim` (`BallSelection`, `DifferenceSelection` — "Ambiguous overloads" otherwise, p1).
- **R-PORT-BETA-DATASET — port propagation constants `ewbe.beta_<n>` are defined only on the dataset of the study
  that ran the boundary-mode steps (round 22, p1/p2).** On `directional_coupler` they read on `dset1` (std1, the
  four bma steps + frequency step) and are "undefined" on dset5 (std3 mode expansion); `Interp` of the field is
  likewise undefined on a dataset whose solution holds no field. Map dataset → solution first (`dataset().getString
  ("solution")`), or pick the dataset by the maximum finite sum of the field (run2).
- **R-PLIST-RANGE — a parametric sweep list set as a space-separated string (`"400[nm] 475[nm] …"`) via
  `setIndex("plistarr", …, 0)` runs ONE value (round 22, run1: 1 wavelength solved, `looplevel` then rejected
  "1".."5").** Use the `range(400[nm],75[nm],700[nm])` string (run2), or set the `plistarr` element per index.
- **R-INTERP-PER-SOLUTION — the property that selects one solution of a parametric dataset for `Interp` is not
  `innerinput` ("Unknown property", run1); discover it at run time among `solnum` / `innersolnum` / `outersolnum` /
  `looplevel` by try/except and log the node's `properties()` (run2).** Related: R-INTERP-SHAPE-MULTI.
- **R-SEED-PARAM-SEMANTICS — a control that changes a seed parameter whose geometric meaning was not verified in the
  seed's own Java text is not a control (round 22, run1).** `directional_coupler` d 3 → 6 µm moved Δn by only −3 %
  and left F(exit) at 0.51 (the seed builds the cores from `d` in a way the round did not verify); the next guess,
  `dn` 0.005 → 0.02, did not converge (stationary solver rel. error 0.18, run2). The control that closed (run3) is the
  device length `len` 2.1 → 0.7 mm, whose effect is PREDICTED from the unchanged port betas: F(exit) 0.218 vs
  sin²(π·len/L_beat) 0.211. Rule: a control's expected value is derived from the seed's geometry sequence and a
  closed form, not from the parameter's description string; both earlier attempts are REPORTed (A-R2).
- **R-NOISE-FLOOR-RATIO — semiconductor terminal currents sit on a ≈1e-13 A solver floor at zero bias; any point-wise
  ratio (conservation |ΣI|/|I_E|, gain I_C/I_B) taken there measures the floor (round 22, run1: conservation 2.2,
  "β_peak" 575 at 1e-13 A while the plateau is 133).** Normalise conservation by the full-scale current and take β
  only where |I_C| exceeds a threshold (1 nA, run2); the seed's own gain plot does the same implicitly by its axis.
- **R-MIE-RULER — a closed-form ruler written from memory is verified against an independent code before it rules
  (round 22).** `22_3D-seed-figures/mie_ruler.py` (Bohren–Huffman) was cross-checked to five decimals against
  `miepython.efficiencies_mx(complex(n, -k), x)`; the "published" reference values the author remembered were
  wrong and the first self-check FAILED on the ruler, not the physics. Convention: pass k = −imag(n_gold) from the
  model (COMSOL n − jk under e^{+jωt}); σ = Q·πr² with x = 2πr n_host/λ₀.

- **R-DG-LEGACY-NOOP — `physics().create("dg","DeformedGeometry",geom)` is a GUI-compatibility shell in 6.2; it never
  moves the mesh (round 24, U25).** Its default `fix1`/`free`/`disp1` features and a `PrescribedNormalMeshVelocity` (`vn`)
  are created and the study lists `dg` as active, yet the boundary coordinate stays at x0 for 7200 s (dx/dt ≈ 5e-20) with
  geometric nonlinearity on or off and `dg.dx` is undefined (`24_…/run2_u25.log`, `probe/p10–p12`). A model that solves
  without error on this route can still pass a self-referential gate (C_i/C* at the frozen x0 matched "exactly") — the
  boundary-position gate is the one that tells.
- **R-DG-COMMON-ROUTE — the working Deformed Geometry in 6.2 lives under Definitions:
  `comp.common().create(tag, "DeformingDomainDeformedGeometry")` (domain), `"FixedBoundaryDeformedGeometry"` (fixed
  boundary), `"PrescribedNormalMeshVelocityDeformedGeometry"` with property `prescribedNormalVelocity` (NOT `vn`).**
  Read from the seed `COMSOL_Multiphysics/Chemical_Engineering/chemical_etching.mph` (903 kB) and
  `electrochemical_polishing.mph` as java text (R-LIB-PREVIEW); the solver's Variables feature then carries
  `comp1_material_disp` ("Material Mesh Displacement (comp1.material.disp)") beside `comp1_c` — the positive control that
  the mesh is solved for. A 1D tds + moving-interface Deal–Grove model then matches the closed form to 0.03 % (`run3–run5_u25.log`,
  `probe/p20–p23`). Type names `FixedMeshDeformedGeometry`, `FixedDeformedGeometry`, `FixedMesh` raise "cannot be created
  in this context".
- **R-COMMON-ACCESSOR — a `common()` child is fetched with `common().get(tag)`** (round 24, `probe/p21_common_dg.log`
  exercises the working path) — unlike `physics(tag)`/`mesh(tag)`. The negative paths (`common(tag)` "not callable",
  `.feature(tag)` no such attribute) are the executing agent's report from its first two attempts, recorded in the
  script docstring only — not in a stored log; treat them as unverified until re-measured.
- **R-DISABLEDPHYSICS-ADVANCED — `disabledphysics=[…]` on a study step is a silent no-op unless `useadvanceddisable=True` is
  set on the same step** (round 24, U24: the predep Dirichlet stayed active through the drive-in, dose ratio 8.55 instead of
  1.00, `run2_u24.log`, `probe/p5_isolate_disable.py`; 1.0000 from `run3` on).
- **R-TRANSIENT-RESOLVE-STALE-INIT — re-running an already-solved Time Dependent study after changing the mesh OR `rtol`
  (either alone) can fail with "Failed to find consistent initial values", while a fresh model at the same settings
  converges** (round 24, `run3–run6_u24.log`, `probe/p14_consistent_init_props.py`). Set
  `m.sol(<sol of that study>).feature("t1").set("consistent","off")` before the re-solve (default `bweuler`); map study →
  solver tag through the `st1` feature's `study` property, never by assuming `sol<n>` ↔ `std<n>`.
- **R-NUMPY-TRAPZ — `numpy.trapz` is gone in numpy ≥ 2.0 on this machine; use `np.trapezoid`** (round 24, `run3_u26.log`).
- **R-HT-DEFAULTS — `ht` default domain feature is `solid1` (`k_mat`/`k`, `rho_mat`/`rho`, `Cp_mat`/`Cp` settable directly,
  no material node needed), `init1` (`Tinit`), and `axi1` is auto-created for `geom.axisymmetric(true)`;
  `SurfaceToAmbientRadiation` reads its OWN `Tamb_src`/`Tamb` (default 293.15 K) — the physics-level `AmbientSettings.T_amb`
  does not reach it** (round 24, `probe/p2_ht_discover.py`, `run3–run5_u26.log`).
- **R-SOLID-DEFAULTS — `solid` default domain feature is `lemm1`; a point `Displacement0` in 2D-axi takes `Direction`/`U0`
  as 3-element STRING arrays (`["0","1","0"]` pins w only) — 2-element, boolean or int arrays hit "Ambiguous overloads";
  a rectangle corner vertex is selectable by a dim-0 `BoxSelection` (R-SEL at `entitydim=0`)** (round 24,
  `probe/p3_solid_discover.py` p3c–p3e, `u27_film_stress_stoney.py`).
- **R-MULTI-MATERIAL-ELASTIC — a film/substrate build uses ONE `lemm1`+`te1` pair reading E, ν, α per domain from the
  material nodes (`Enu` group, `def.thermalexpansioncoefficient`), the `layered_plate.mph` pattern — not one
  `LinearElasticModel` per material** (round 24, `seed/layered_plate.java`, `u27`).
- **R-MESH-SEL-DIM — `mesh.feature("map1").selection().all()` needs `selection().geom("geom1", JInt(2))` first ("No entity
  dimension specified"); `FreeTri` does not** (round 24, `run1_u27.log`) — feature-type dependent.
- **R-SOLID-ASPECT-SOLVER — a mapped mesh with ~250:1 element aspect (1 µm film on a 10 mm disk) fails the default
  Stationary solver ("relative error 0.08 > tolerance") on LINEAR elasticity; force the auto sequence's `Direct` to
  `linsolver="pardiso"` and set `FullyCoupled` `maxiter=50`, `termonres="off"` — same mesh then converges and a 2× finer
  mesh moves κ by 0.0003 %** (round 24, `run2_u27.log` → `run3_u27.log`).
- **R-CURVATURE-SIGN — derive the sign of a fitted parabola's curvature (`κ = d²w/dr² = 2·c2`), never guess it (round 24,
  `run3_u27.log`: magnitude within 0.7 %, sign flipped, every κ gate FAILed at ~199 %); a magnitude-agrees/sign-disagrees
  pattern is a READOUT convention bug, not a model defect.** The plot code must use the same expression as the gate —
  run4's PNG still carried the discarded sign and was rebuilt by `probe/p9`.
- **R-GAUSSIAN-SLOPE-RULER-BIAS — a `ln C` vs `x²` slope measures 4Dt only when the drive-in kernel is much wider than the
  starting profile; at D3·t2/(D1·t1) ≈ 7 the profile is not Gaussian and the slope is a BIASED ruler (stable −7.4 % across
  three runs at different mesh/rtol — R-ISOLATE says the numerics are not the cause)** (round 24, `run3–run5_u24.log`).
  Use the exact mirror-convolution reference, or a one-parameter Dt least-squares fit against that family (`run6_u24.log`:
  −0.007 % / −0.097 %); the biased number is kept as REPORT.
- **R-INSTANT-SLOPE-WINDOW — an "initial slope" gate compares a WINDOW fit of the model with the SAME window fit of the
  closed form, never with the closed form's t = 0 derivative** (round 24, `run3–run4_u25.log`: the Deal–Grove curve is
  concave over 180 s, so its own window fit is 7.00 % below B/(A+2x0) while the model matches the window fit to 0.011 %;
  gate redefined in `run5_u25.log`).
- **R-UNIT-RELABEL — feeding bare "pretend µm / µm²/s / cm⁻³" numbers with the geometry left in metres and `tds` in mol/m³
  is internally consistent for a linear PDE (round 24, U24/U25: every gate agrees with the identically relabelled
  reference), but every native figure and table then carries SI labels that are false ("Arc length (m)", "mol/m³")** —
  either set `geom.lengthUnit` and real units, or state the relabelling in every caption (`out/u24_fig_profiles_native.png`).

- **R-TLIST-QUADRATURE — a time-integrated balance (energy, charge, dose) is only as good as the STORED output grid: the
  seed `laser_heating_wafer` at its shipped `tlist range(0,1,60)` gives an energy-balance error of +3.99 % by trapezoid
  (+1.83 % Simpson) that a `range(0,0.1,60)` re-solve of the SAME physics closes to +0.028 %** (round 24, `run5_u26.log`,
  `probe/p4b_s2_dense_tlist.py`: 42 s, 601 samples; the 61-point subsample of the dense solution reproduces +3.99 %).
  Densify `tlist` before gating a time integral; a `timeint()` operator is not the fix (next rule). Read the time axis
  with the expression `t`, never as the sample index.
- **R-TIMEINT-3D-HANG — `timeint(0,60,intop(...))` at its DEFAULT tolerance (tol 1e-8, minlen 1e-4) in an `EvalGlobal`
  on a 3D transient dataset (4 k DOF, 61 stored steps, moving T⁴ integrand) did not return in 45 min (flat CPU) and had
  to be killed; the same call with explicit bounds `timeint(0,60,expr,1e-2,1e-2)` returned in ~24 s and closed the
  energy balance to +0.008 %** (round 24, `probe/p4_s2_isolation.py`, `probe/p4_result.json`; syntax from the local
  `COMSOL_ReferenceManual.pdf` p.323–324). Evidence trail for the hang: the main session's process listing at 18:47
  (python PID started 18:01, `p4.log` last line 18:02:52, killed 18:52 — ledger row 9 of the round's session) and the
  docstring of `probe/p4b_s2_dense_tlist.py`; the hung run's own log was overwritten by the bounded retry, so the
  duration is an in-session observation, not a stored log line. A nested spatial coupling operator is accepted as `expr`. JPype cannot cancel
  an in-flight Java call — a hung `timeint` costs the process. Prefer the dense-`tlist` route (previous rule) or the
  bounded form; never the default tolerance on a 3D transient.

<!-- Process-layer rules written back after round 24 (2026-09-15): each names the round-24 event that measured it. -->
- **R-SEED-CARRIES-MECHANISM — a seed named in a work card is text-verified to CONTAIN the mechanism under test before
  the card is issued; a mechanism that shows no effect after 3 probes goes seed-first, not probe-deeper** (round 24, U25).
  `work-card_AB.md` named `oxide_jacking.mph` as the moving-boundary seed; it has no moving boundary. Nine scratch probes
  (`probe/p2_seed_movingboundary.log` … `probe/p10_isolate_dg_notmoving.log`) reproduced zero interface motion before
  `probe/p20_seed_chemetch.log` grepped `chemical_etching.java` and `probe/p21_common_dg.log` found the working node type
  in one step. The check is one grep of the seed's `.java` text (`model.java.save(path,"java")`, R-SAVE-JAVA) for the
  feature type the card relies on; R-LIB-PREVIEW (size) is necessary, not sufficient.
- **R-RULER-SELF-TEST — before a gate rules on a model, its ruler is run on the closed form's OWN samples (synthetic
  data at the gate's grid/window) and must return the input within the gate tolerance; a ruler that fails the self-test
  is a defect of the card, not a FAIL of the model** (round 24). Two gates failed for this reason with zero physics wrong:
  U24 A-G5 (`ln C` vs `x²` slope, −7.4 %, `run6_u24.log` line `A-G5_biased_ruler_REPORT`) and U25 B-G3 (180 s window fit
  compared with the t = 0 derivative, −6.99 %, `run4_u25.log` line 13). Both would have surfaced in seconds of numpy;
  together they cost 3 COMSOL runs and one gate redefinition each (R-GAUSSIAN-SLOPE-RULER-BIAS, R-INSTANT-SLOPE-WINDOW
  are the specific cases). Extends R-MIE-RULER (which checks the closed form; this checks the estimator).
- **R-REDEFINED-GATE-REPORT — a redefined gate keeps its superseded ruler in the script as a `REPORT` line so the FINAL
  run log carries both numbers; a README sentence is not a substitute** (round 24). U24 did this
  (`run6_u24.log`: `A-G5_biased_ruler_REPORT` −7.4 % beside A-G5a/b PASS); U26 did not — the +3.99 % C-S2 quadrature
  number exists only in `run5_u26.log` lines 46–47, and `run6_u26.log` shows +0.028 % with no trace of what it replaced
  (code-reviewer finding, ledger row 10 of the round's session). The audit trail must survive on the log the verdict cites.
- **R-FIG-FROM-GATE-VARS — a figure is drawn from the SAME variables the gate ruled on, never from a recomputation in
  the plotting code; when only the drawing is wrong, regenerate from stored data without a re-solve** (round 24, U27).
  `run4_u27.log` gated κ = 2·c₂ (PASS +0.70 %) while the plot block still used the discarded −κ draft, so
  `out/u27_fig_bow.png` showed the Stoney parabola inverted against the model points; `probe/p9_replot_u26_u27.py`
  redrew it from `out/u27_result.json` + `out/u27_wr.txt` in 2 s (ledger row 4). A figure that contradicts its own
  gate line is a `figure-self-read` failure (rule file `~/.claude/rules/figure-self-read.md`).
- **R-RESULT-JSON-SCHEMA — every item's `out/<item>_result.json` follows the skeleton contract: top-level `round`,
  `item`, `inputs`, `gates` (list of `"PASS|FAIL|UNDET|REPORT  <id>: <text>"` lines, identical to the log lines),
  `fails`, `undet`, `verdict`, `timings_s`; per-gate numbers may be added under their own keys but never REPLACE
  `gates`** (round 24). Four scripts wrote four shapes — `u24_result.json` keyed by gate id, `u25_result.json` with
  `gates`, `u26_result.json` nested under `text`/`seed`, `u27_result.json` flat scalars — and `build_viewer.py` raised
  `KeyError: 'gates'` and had to fall back to regex-parsing the four final logs. A page builder or inventory script
  reads the json; the log is the audit copy. `references/script-skeleton.py` carries the keys.
- **R-PROBE-TIMEOUT — every background run or probe carries a wall-clock cap of 10× the measured solve time of the same
  model (floor 5 min); no new log line past the cap is a hang, not a slow run: kill the Python PID AND its
  `comsolmphserver.exe` child (JPype cannot cancel an in-flight Java call), log the kill in the ledger, and keep the hung
  run's log under its own name** (round 24). `probe/p4.log` stopped at 18:02:52 on a model that solves in 60 s and was
  found at 18:47 by a process listing, not by a cap (ledger row 9); its log was then overwritten by the bounded retry,
  so the 45 min hang survives only as an in-session observation (R-TIMEINT-3D-HANG evidence note). A cap would have
  returned the same diagnosis at ~18:13.
- **R-CONCURRENT-SESSIONS — two `mph.start(cores=8)` sessions from two agents ran concurrently on this machine without a
  licence clash** (round 24, measured): `run1_u24.log` 17:22:36–17:22:56 overlaps `run1_u26.log` 17:22:29–17:22:54;
  `run5_u24.log` and `run1_u27.log` both start 17:38:53; the overlap lasted the whole A/B vs C/D dispatch (17:22–17:56).
  Not measured: the per-run slowdown from 16 requested cores on 16 logical, and the licence-retry path (never
  exercised). Two-agent dispatch is therefore allowed; a third session is a guess until measured.
- **R-EXECUTOR-RESUMABLE — an executor agent can die mid-card, and the successor resumes from the last `runN.log` +
  `out/` + `probe/`, never from run 1** (round 24): the A/B work-card executor was terminated by an API authorization
  error (`oauth_org_not_allowed`, HTTP 403, model `claude-sonnet-5`) after `run5_u24.log` (17:39) and `run2_u25.log`
  (17:56); two testing-bug-fixer agents resumed at `run6_u24.log` (18:33) and `run3_u25.log` (18:37) from the logs alone
  (ledger row 6). Two obligations follow: (1) every attempt writes its own numbered log and `out/` files as it goes —
  nothing lives only in the agent's context; (2) the model named for a dispatched executor is one the organisation
  allows, checked by the dispatcher before the card goes out — the 403 is silent until the agent is already dead.
- **R-DG-NATIVE-1D-FRAME — under a `common()` Deformed Geometry (R-DG-COMMON-ROUTE) a native 1D `LineGraph` `Image`
  export plots its x-axis on the MESH (reference) frame: `out/u25_fig_xt_native.png` spans 0–0.02 while the interface
  moved ~0.5 in the same units, so the motion is invisible** (round 24, observed; fix UNVERIFIED). Candidate fix: set
  the graph's `xdata` to the expression `x` (spatial frame) — not yet run. Until measured, a native 1D figure of a
  moving-boundary model is labelled "mesh frame" in its caption and the matplotlib redraw from the Data export is the
  audience figure (`out/u25_fig_xt.png`).
- **R-DEPOSIT-MPH — a round that calls `.solve()` deposits at least one solved `.mph` in `out/`, and the deposit
  shape is checked by an instrument, not remembered** (round 25). Round 25 shipped complete on every other axis and
  still had no `.mph`: the script simply never called `model.save()`, and nothing read the emitted folder to notice.
  The rule is therefore a property of the ASSET — *a gated round folder must contain X* — enforced by
  `tools/deposit_gate.py`, which reads the emitted folder (never the producer's own state) and checks D1 README,
  D2 frontmatter (`layer`/`audience`/`verdict`), D3 `run*.log`, D4 non-empty `out/`, D5 a `*result*.json`, D6 the
  `.mph`. D6's predicate is CONDITIONAL on evidence inside the folder (`.solve(` appears in one of its scripts),
  never on the folder's name or number — a position-free predicate, so a post-processing-only round passes instead
  of being retro-failed. `--self-test` runs both controls and exits 2 (instrument fault, worse than any FAIL) unless
  removing the `.mph` from a known-good round flips D6 **and only D6**. Measured on the whole rig the day it was
  written: 16 gated rounds, 13 folders correctly SKIPped as non-rounds, exactly one FAIL (round 25, the round that
  motivated it) — a first run that fails on the known defect and nothing else is the positive control for the sweep.
  Cost note: an `.mph` from a 40 k-element mode-analysis round with 8 eigenvalues is **58.6 MB**, so a round saves the
  claim-bearing cases, not every swept point (round 25 ruling: 3 of 9; the other 6 differ by one parameter and their
  numbers are in the result json).
- **R-GATE-NO-INVENTED-CONVENTION — a deposit check may only enforce a convention the rig actually decided.**
  Two header checks were written into `deposit_gate.py` and both failed their own positive control: `%`-only
  (9 of 16 rounds use `#`), then `% or #` (round 07 uses a bare column-name row). Three styles coexist across the
  closed rounds, so there is no convention to enforce — only one the checker would be inventing, after which closed
  rounds would be retro-failed by a rule they were never built against. The check was DELETED rather than tuned a
  third time, and the header convention registered as an open question for the user. A positive control that fails
  means the ruler is wrong, not the artifact.
- **R-GATE-ROUND-BY-EVIDENCE — membership of a gated class is decided by EVIDENCE OF A RUN inside the folder, and
  a widened predicate is measured against the whole corpus BEFORE it ships** (round 27; both halves measured the
  same day). The bug: `deposit_gate.py` predicated "is this a round?" on `folder.glob("run*.log")`; round 27 named
  its logs `partB_run1.log`, so the gate printed SKIP and exited 0 — a real deposit escaped gating while the
  instrument reported success, which is worse than a FAIL because it reads as coverage. **The first fix was wrong
  and is the more useful half of this rule**: it promoted "a folder named `^\d{2}_` IS a round; no log is then a
  FAIL", which is a NAME predicate, not evidence — swept over the rig it turned **10 correct SKIPs into false
  FAILs** (`00_source`, both briefs, `04_reference-models`, `05_provenance-audit`, `06_feasibility-probe`,
  `09_capability-inventory`, `20_manual-and-report`, `23_showcase` are sources, registers and deliverables with no
  run to gate). That is R-GATE-NO-INVENTED-CONVENTION again, one severity level up instead of down, and it was
  caught only because the sweep was re-run over already-delivered folders — the standing "run a new gate over the
  existing corpus first" habit is what separated it from a shipped regression. The correct predicate has two
  evidence branches, each counted across all 31 folders before adoption: (a) a log matching `*run*.log` — fires on
  all 18 real rounds and no non-round; (b) an `out/` carrying a `*result*.json` or `.mph` with no log at all — the
  misnamed-log escape, 0 false fires across the 13 non-rounds. Three regression cases in `--self-test`:
  `99_escape-case` (prefixed log names), `97_results-but-no-log` (must FAIL on D3 specifically), and two
  **over-fire** cases (`96_source-material`, `95_capability-register`: numbered, no run evidence, must SKIP) which
  exist so the name predicate cannot come back. Final sweep: 18 gated / 18 complete / 13 skipped.
- **R-EWBE-K1-NEEDS-N-VARIABLE — the `n` in an `ewbe` wave vector `k1 = k*n` is a DOMAIN-SCOPED VARIABLE the model
  defines itself, not a material property** (round 27). Without it the solve stops at `Undefined variable n`; and the
  background and override variable selections must NOT overlap or compile fails with
  `Duplicate parameter/variable name`. Seed form: `prop("WaveVector").set("dirCount", "UniDirectionality")` +
  `set("k1", {"k*n","0","0"})`.
- **R-MAT-REFRACTIVE-INDEX-GROUP — the property group tag must be `RefractiveIndex`, its type `Refractive_index`
  (underscore), and the values one-element String arrays** (round 27). A wrong tag raises NOTHING at build time; it
  surfaces at solve time as `Undefined material property 'n'`. The index is a SCALAR — passing a 9-component tensor
  gives `A scalar value expected`.
- **R-EWBE-NEEDS-PML-NOT-MBC — a Matched BC on a wall PARALLEL to the propagation direction barely absorbs** (round
  27, measured): wall power 6.10 / 4.25 / 0.55 % at half-heights 80 / 160 / 320 µm, with total power not conserved
  plane to plane (0.66 → 2.33 %). A layered PML rectangle gives 0.0007 %. Its `wavelengthSource` can only be set
  AFTER the physics exists (`coordSystem("pml1").set("wavelengthSource", "ewbe")`).
- **R-GEOM-INTERSECTION-NOT-PARTITION — `Intersection` consumes the circle; `Partition` leaves it in the union and
  cuts other objects with it** (round 27). Also: the resulting domain COUNT is measured, never guessed — 6 with the
  baffles, 2 without, against the 4 that was assumed.
- **R-EXPORT-PLOT-PROPS — a `result().export()` node of type `Plot` addresses its source with `plotgroup` + `plot`,
  not `sourceplot`** (round 27; `sourceplot` raises `Unknown property: sourceplot`). It carries its own boolean
  `anythingwritten`, read beside the file size that R-EXPORT-PLOT-TEXT already requires.
- **R-EXPORT-PLOT-ABSCISSA-UNIT — the first column of a `Plot` text export is the cut line's ARC LENGTH in the unit
  the PLOT AXIS declares (header `% Arc length (mm)`), which is neither metres nor the model's geometry unit**
  (round 27). The seed's geometry is in µm and its export in mm. Read as metres, every abscissa printed 1000× too
  large and NOTHING flagged it — every comparison in the reader was between two quantities carrying the same wrong
  factor, so a common factor cancels and stays invisible. The header is the only place the unit exists: parse it,
  and treat an unconvertible unit as an instrument fault rather than defaulting to one. (Distinct from
  R-INTERP-COORDS-IN-GEOMETRY-UNITS, which governs coordinates going IN; this governs the abscissa coming OUT.)
- **R-CONTROL-READ-THE-SEED-ITS-OWN-WAY — when a shipped verification model is used as the known-good control, read
  it through ITS OWN datasets and plot expressions, not a fresh `Interp` grid** (round 27). A fresh grid over
  `focusing_lens`'s ewbe solution returned a spatially uniform ~1.0 V/m — an idle baseline, so the control was
  unreadable and the round had to stand at UNDET. Through the seed's own `CutLine2D` + native Plot export the same
  solution reads as a clear focus (on-axis peak 3.229 at x = 907 µm against its stated f = 940 µm; focal-plane
  intensity FWHM 8.07 µm against the closed form 0.8859·λf/D = 8.33 µm, −3.1 %). The seed carries the apparatus it
  was designed to be read with; building a second one is a new instrument that needs its own calibration.
- **R-SEMI-RESERVED-PARAMS — the `Semiconductor` interface reserves the parameter names `R` and `Rm`** (round 28,
  runs 1-2). A model parameter called `R` (outer radius) or `Rm` (mirror reflectance) compiles the geometry, the
  materials, the doping and the mesh without complaint and then dies at `Compile Equations: Semiconductor
  Equilibrium` with `Duplicate parameter/variable name - Variable: R - Geometry: geom1 - Points: 1, 12-14, ...`.
  The message points at GEOMETRY POINTS, not at the parameter, so it reads like a geometry fault. `semi` defines
  `R` (net recombination rate) and `Rm` over every semiconductor point. Rename (`r_out`, `R_mir`). This extends the
  single-letter reserved list (`h s w t`) to two-letter physics variables: any short name a physics interface
  publishes as a field variable is unusable as a parameter, and the failure surfaces only at compile time.
- **R-UDGENERATION — the user-defined optical/radiation generation feature is `UDGeneration` with properties `Gn`
  and `Gp`** (round 28). `UserDefinedGeneration`, `UserDefinedRecombination`, `AdditionalGeneration`,
  `DirectRecombination` and `AugerRecombination` all raise `Unknown feature ID` at both the physics level and under
  `smm1`; only `OpticalTransitions` and `TrapAssistedRecombination` exist under the names the GUI suggests. The id
  was read out of the seeds `si_solar_cell_1d.mph` and `pin_radiation_effects.mph` via `model.java.save(path,
  "java")` - the cheap route whenever a GUI node name does not map to a feature id.
- **R-MESH-SELECTION-NEEDS-DIM — a mesh feature's `selection().all()` fails with `No entity dimension specified`
  until `selection().geom("geom1", jpype.JInt(dim))` is called first** (round 28, `Map` in 2D). Physics features
  accept a bare `.all()`; mesh features do not.
- **R-RULER-BEFORE-MODEL-ON-UNDET — when a gate reads UNDET, suspect the closed form before the model** (round 28,
  run4: BOTH UNDET lines were the ruler). (1) A revolved-volume check compared against `pi*r_a^2*t` and read
  -3.1 %; the top 20 nm layer reaches only `r_c`, and the corrected `pi(r_a^2*300nm + r_c^2*20nm)` matched to
  0.0000 % for all three variants. (2) A geometry-sensitivity control sampled |E| 10 nm inside the absorber-mesa
  sidewall and returned the same value to 9 digits for every variant - not an insensitive model but an observable
  with no sensitivity by construction (the stack is laterally uniform there and the depletion never reaches it).
  Re-aimed at a FIXED absolute radius that lies under the collector mesa for one variant and outside it for
  another, the same control fired at 88 %. A control that cannot separate is a statement about the ruler until the
  ruler has been checked against a quantity the geometry provably moves.
- **R-SEMI-ZERO-BIAS-FLOOR — a `semi` stationary solution carries a non-zero terminal current at zero bias; any
  slope ruler on low currents must mask it** (round 30, Fig. 7 run1). The 2D-axi PD read |I| = 3.3e-15 A at
  Va = 0 at every lifetime. An ideality fit on 0.15-0.35 V of a curve that sat on that floor (tau = 1 ms) read
  n = 1.49 and made a control go UNDET. Read `|I(0)|` in the same sweep and fit only points above 100x it.
- **R-HOMOJUNCTION-PREMISE — "switch SRH off and the diffusion current (n = 1) takes over" is a homojunction
  premise; in a double heterostructure it can be false** (round 30, Fig. 7). With wide-gap layers on both sides of
  the InGaAs, minority carriers cannot diffuse to the contacts, so every forward current recombines with the same
  tau: I(V; tau_a)/I(V; tau_b) = tau_b/tau_a to 1.3 % at 0.4-0.6 V, n stays ~1.6 at tau = 1 ms. Test the
  premise with a 1/tau scaling check at several forward biases before building a control on it.
- **R-ZERO-THICKNESS-RECT — a swept layer thickness of 0 makes a `Rectangle` size invalid** ("Elements must
  satisfy: x > 0", round 30 f6b attempt 1). Start thickness sweeps at a small positive value (round 08 used 10 nm),
  and make sure the list contains the operating point the gate reads (attempt 2 stepped past 200 nm).
- **R-INTERP-FUNC-TABLE — a 1D `Interpolation` function fed from Python** (round 30, measured OK first try):
  `func().create(t, "Interpolation")`, `set("funcname", name)`, `set("table", JArray(JArray(JString))(rows))`
  with rows of `[arg, value]` strings, `setIndex("argunit", "nm", 0)`, `setIndex("fununit", "1/m", 0)`,
  `set("extrap", "const")`. Called as `name(z)` the SI coordinate is converted to the declared arg unit. Re-setting
  `table` between solves swaps the profile without rebuilding (4 wavelengths, q*intG = q*P*A/hv to 0.00 %).
